D1: DB enum model_engine: members are interpolated in the migration (f-string / variable list); membership checks skipped for it
DB enum prompt_type: members are interpolated in the migration (f-string / variable list); membership checks skipped for it
SQLAlchemy Core select()/update() by attribute is a model consumer, not a raw-SQL consumer; attribute misuse there is caught by python, not by this index
f-string SQL: interpolated table/column names appear as '{}' and are not checked
raw SQL column extraction handles INSERT column lists, UPDATE SET lists, and single-table WHERE/SELECT lists only; multi-table joins are indexed as table consumers but their columns are not checked
D2: frontend HTTP method is inferred from apiClient.<verb> on the same/previous 3 lines; URLs built in helpers are attributed to the literal's line, with method assumed GET when not visible
request-body key checks run only where the body is an inline object literal in the same call; bodies built in variables are not checked
response_model expressions like ApiResponse[List[X]] are matched by token, not evaluated
D3: `.delay(*args, **kwargs)` forwarding is marked '**' and not arity-checked
default task names are derived as <module path>.<func> relative to the package root; if Celery's `include` uses a different module path the derived name may differ from the registered one
producers with dynamic task names (variables, f-strings) are listed as suspect, not checked
D4: TS scanning is regex per line: multi-line object literals and template-built values are missed; type-guard helpers (isX(...)) are invisible
f-string values, variables and getattr() strings are invisible to the membership check
generic slot names (name, type, status, id, ...) are excluded from slot ownership to keep noise down; vocabularies whose only slot is generic get no undeclared-literal check

slot binding is by name: a literal is checked only when it sits in a keyword argument, dict key, comparison or assignment whose name is a slot owned by a vocabulary (DB column names typed by the enum, typed pydantic/dataclass/TS fields, snake_case of the enum class); literals passed positionally are indexed as consumers but not membership-checked
D5: BaseSettings fields are read as upper-cased field names; a pydantic env_prefix is not applied

node .env files (.env.node01 etc.) are gitignored and were NOT read (dev/CLAUDE.md §3 forbids printing .env.node01); declarations come from compose environment: blocks, ${VAR:-default} interpolations, .env*.example, Dockerfile ENV, configs/
worker config helpers are matched by name (_env, _get_env, ...); a helper with another name hides its keys
D6: SeaweedFS path conventions are not indexed (no single definition site was found to anchor them)
def/call orphan analysis counts any Name/Attribute reference by bare name; a method sharing its name with a common attribute (get, run, ...) is never reported, so the orphan list is an under-count
engine server request/response shapes (ivgs-workers/servers/*) are indexed as routes (D2 rows with app=ivgs-workers/<server>); their clients are matched by URL tail only where the tail is a literal
D7: TS types are parsed by regex (ts-morph is not in the frontend toolchain): generics, mapped types, unions of object types and index signatures are approximated
TS<->pydantic links exist only where the frontend call's generic type and the route's response_model both name an indexed type; name-based links are marked as such
field-usage counts are bare-name matches across src/, so a field named like a common word (id, name, status) is never reported as dead
